page: Microsoft Azure D4als_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine profile within the Dalv6 series, configured with a low-memory 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. The memory configuration totals 8.0 GB (2.0 GB per vCPU). The instance does not bundle any physical GPUs or ephemeral local storage, requiring remote network-attached disks for operating system and data persistence.

Benchmark evaluation highlights robust single-core compute capability, with top-quartile results across stress-ng single-core execution (3079.67) and Geekbench 6 single-core tests (2077.0). Multi-threaded compute metrics remain within the median range, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 4753.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 7558.85. The instruction set features AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) along with AES and SHA cryptographic accelerations.

Resource tradeoffs center primarily on the constrained memory footprint and memory subsystems. Large-block memory read bandwidth reached 36.9 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% of measured instances, and PassMark memory performance scored in the lowest 10% (1098.32). Similarly, database operations scored in the bottom quartile, and 7B parameter LLM inference speeds dropped significantly due to memory throughput limits. Conversely, the instance sustained 6.18 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.57 GB/sec static web throughput.

From an infrastructure cost efficiency standpoint, D4als_v6 offers an economical dedicated-core AMD deployment for organizations that need elevated clock speeds and solid single-thread performance without paying for surplus RAM. Best-fit deployments include front-end web serving, microservices, containerized application nodes, text processing, and batch tasks that stay comfortably within an 8 GB operational envelope.
description: Microsoft Azure D4als_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical AMD EPYC 9V74 cores operating at 3.7 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. It does not include bundled local storage or hardware GPU accelerators. The instance delivers strong single-core CPU throughput, reaching top-quartile results in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core benchmarks, supported by AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction extensions. Memory bandwidth and capacity are strictly bounded, leading to lower comparative throughput in large-scale database operations and multi-gigabyte in-memory processing. With an average static web throughput of 6.57 GB/sec and 6.18 million Redis operations per second, D4als_v6 represents a cost-efficient hardware profile for compute-driven, memory-lean enterprise services, API endpoints, microservices, and lightweight batch processing tasks.
